title: Different priors, same data
sub: Posterior beliefs about a coin's bias, for three priors, as flips accumulate.

frames.caption: Three people judge the same coin with different priors. Blue thinks every bias is equally likely. Orange is sure coins are nearly fair. Aqua expects heads-heavy coins. Their prior means range from 0.50 to 0.82.
After 10 flips (5 heads), everyone updates with the same likelihood. Blue moves furthest, since it believed least to begin with; the skeptic barely budges.
50 flips (30 heads). The posteriors are pulling together: the means now differ by 0.08.

500 flips (300 heads). The three posteriors almost coincide around the true bias of 0.6 (dashed): their means differ by just 0.012. With enough data the likelihood swamps any prior that does not rule the truth out completely. The prior matters most exactly when data are scarce.
